Dear Jack,

Hope you are well.

Further to the voicemail I just left on your phone, please see the attached drawings for a single storey rear extension at 208 Newbridge Road in Bath, BA13LF.

The proposed rear extension comprises a warm flat roof, with shallow falls (expressed internally) of around 5 to 8 degrees. There are three facets to the roof, including one ridge and two valleys, although subject to design requirements, I'm not sure the valley channels are strictly required, and there may be a more sensible way to fall to the designated RWP outlets. The roof is inset behind a perimeter parapet, and to keep costs down, we would like to explore a single ply membrane with a mid-grey finish, to tie in with the Natural Zinc parapet.

At my previous office (CaSA Architects in Bath) we specified SIG roofing products on a number of flat roof projects, and as I understand it you were able to provide product specifications as well as technical input, including drainage calcs and thermal performance. Is this something you could provide here? Subject to a work in progress SAP assessment, we are targeting an overall U-Value of 0.13 W/m2K, so it would be great if you could provide insulation requirements too.

At the same time I would like to try and persuade the client to consider a sedum roof finish, however the budget is tight, and I'm not sure they will be able to stretch that far in the first instance - is it something that could be designed in now, but installed at a later date?

Please let me know if you are able assist and please feel free to call if it's easier to chat in the first instance?

Kind regards,

Ian Darlington
Architect

STUDIO STACKYARD

body_excerpt:
Good afternoon,

Can I request a tapered design and pricing on this please, if this one can be turned around asap as I belive works on site have already begun.

Bit of an odd one, but requirements are as follows.

Tapered insulation to fit in between structural upstands, Max 2.9m between them
Be 1:80 and tapered to each end from the centre
Minimum thickness of scheme, Including the 50mm flat board, of 120mm, to ensure it meets the results of our condensation risk analysis.

Below is some further details from Paul Rimmer of SIG Roofing.

I have attached a roof plan from which we need to secure a price as quick as possible for a CTF scheme in Powerdeck F. As the system is to be installed on Composite panel we need to quote as multi-layer with the
The first layer to be 50mm. The reason is the thickness of the outer sheet on the panel will be 0.5mm, less than the gauge of a minimum thickness steel deck so a pull out test has already been performed by SFS Fasteners and the fixing that passed was a peel rivet, so the 50mm is to be mechanically fixed and the tapered boards will be adhered to the 50mm, the on top tapered boards must be a single layer 1: 80 falls
To restrict the height build up. RTL have already been appointed contractor to this project and works have commenced with removal of roof top plant. There is an indication on the plan of the Structural Upstands
That for the purpose of costing we need to assume would be insulated with Flat 120mm board vertically and across the top. It would probably be better not to include these in the CTF scheme but as a separately quoted item.

Kind regards,
[cid:image001.png@01DD71EC.47468F50]

Jack Rider-Dobson
Regional Specification Manager - South West
